**This is a pre-release for testing.** It is not marked Latest and is not intended for general use. If you want a stable build, use [v0.4.8](https://github.com/samsoir/xearthlayer/releases/tag/v0.4.8).

This is the second build of the 0.5.0 line. It brings a **package manager in the terminal**, much faster package installs that need far less temporary disk space, and the first **signed and notarized macOS** build, now also on Homebrew.

| Platform | Download |
|---|---|
| Linux x86_64 (glibc 2.34 or newer) | `xearthlayer-v0.5.0-alpha.2-x86_64-linux.tar.gz` |
| macOS, Apple Silicon | `xearthlayer-v0.5.0-alpha.2-arm64-macos.tar.gz`, or Homebrew (below) |

No `.deb`, `.rpm` or AUR package is built for previews. There is no Intel Mac build; Intel Mac users can build from source. The `xearthlayer-publish` tarballs are the package publishing tool, which testers do not need.

---

## Setup

Close X-Plane and stop any running XEarthLayer before you start.

### 1. Install the binary

**Linux:**

```bash
tar xzf xearthlayer-v0.5.0-alpha.2-x86_64-linux.tar.gz
mkdir -p ~/.local/bin
mv xearthlayer ~/.local/bin/
xearthlayer --version        # should print 0.5.0-alpha.2
```

**macOS:** install [macFUSE](https://macfuse.io) first, including the one-time approval of its system extension. [docs/macos.md](https://github.com/samsoir/xearthlayer/blob/develop/0.5.0/docs/macos.md) walks through it.

With Homebrew, the pre-release channel follows every alpha, beta and rc build, and `brew upgrade` keeps it current:

```bash
brew install --cask xearthlayer/tap/xearthlayer@prerelease
xearthlayer --version        # should print 0.5.0-alpha.2
```

If macFUSE is already installed from its own installer, add `--skip-cask-deps`.

From the tarball instead: Safari unpacks the download into a folder for you. With Safari:

```bash
cd ~/Downloads/xearthlayer-v0.5.0-alpha.2-arm64-macos
```

With any other browser:

```bash
cd ~/Downloads
tar xzf xearthlayer-v0.5.0-alpha.2-arm64-macos.tar.gz
```

Then:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.local/bin
mv xearthlayer ~/.local/bin/
xearthlayer --version        # should print 0.5.0-alpha.2
```

The binary is signed and notarized, so the `xattr -c` step alpha.1 needed is gone. The first run needs a network connection, because macOS checks the notarization once. If `xearthlayer` is not found, add `export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"` to your shell profile and open a new terminal.

### 2. Coming from alpha.1?

Your configuration, packages and staging library carry over. Bring the configuration up to date, which adds the new settings with their defaults:

```bash
xearthlayer config upgrade
```

Then go to step 5, or straight to step 6 if you already have the regions you fly.

### 3. Coming from v0.4.8, or new to XEarthLayer?

New to XEarthLayer on this machine? Run `xearthlayer setup`. When it finishes it offers to open the package manager; say no for now, do step 4, then continue from step 5.

Coming from v0.4.8: the first command you run copies your `config.ini` to the platform's standard location (`~/.config/xearthlayer/` on Linux, `~/Library/Application Support/XEarthLayer/` on macOS) and may ask you to confirm. Accepting is safe: nothing else is moved, and the old `config.ini` is kept, so v0.4.8 still works if you go back to it. Then:

```bash
xearthlayer config upgrade
```

The rebuilt world replaces the old one, and the two must not be installed together. Remove every old package **before installing anything new**:

```bash
xearthlayer packages remove --all --force
xearthlayer packages remove --all --type overlay --force
xearthlayer packages list    # should report no packages installed
```

If you had no overlays, the second line prints `Error: Package manager error: No overlay packages are installed`, which is harmless. There is nothing to clean up by hand in `Custom Scenery`: XEarthLayer rebuilds its entries there every time it starts.

### 4. Point XEarthLayer at the staging library

Skip this if you came from alpha.1.

```bash
xearthlayer config set packages.library_url https://raw.githubusercontent.com/samsoir/xearthlayer-regional-scenery/staging/xearthlayer_package_library.txt
xearthlayer config set packages.auto_install_overlays true
```

To go back to the stable library later, set it to `https://xearthlayer.app/packages/xearthlayer_package_library.txt`.

### 5. Install the regions you fly

Open the package manager:

```bash
xearthlayer packages
```

Press `2` for the Library, move with the arrow keys, mark regions with `Space`, press `i` and confirm with `y`. Press `3` to watch the downloads and installs. `?` lists every key, and `q` quits. [docs/package-management.md](https://github.com/samsoir/xearthlayer/blob/develop/0.5.0/docs/package-management.md) describes it in full.

The command line works as before, and now takes several regions at once: `xearthlayer packages install na-canada eu-west`. A region code, or the start of one, installs every package beneath it.

| Region | Covers | Download |
|---|---|---|
| `NA-USA-BERMUDA-BAHAMAS` | Contiguous US, Alaska, Hawaii, Bermuda, the Bahamas, Turks and Caicos | 14.1 GB |
| `NA-MEXICO-CENTRAL` | Mexico, Central America and the Caribbean | 4.5 GB |
| `NA-CANADA-WEST` | Canada west of 95° W | 10.2 GB |
| `NA-CANADA-EAST` | Canada east of 95° W | 13.2 GB |
| `NA-GREENLAND` | Greenland | 0.8 GB |
| `SA-WEST` | Colombia, Venezuela, Ecuador, Peru, Bolivia, Chile, the Guianas | 9.2 GB |
| `SA-EAST` | Brazil, Argentina, Paraguay, Uruguay, the Falklands | 8.8 GB |
| `EU-WEST` | Europe west of Russia, Iceland, Scandinavia, the Mediterranean | 16.1 GB |
| `EU-EAST` | European Russia west of the Urals | 3.7 GB |
| `AF-NORTH` | North and West Africa | 7.3 GB |
| `AF-SOUTH` | Central, East and Southern Africa | 9.1 GB |
| `AS-INDIA-MIDDLE-EAST-HIMALAYAN` | Middle East, Central Asia, the Indian subcontinent | 16.8 GB |
| `AS-CHINA-MONGOLIA` | China and Mongolia | 18.5 GB |
| `AS-ASIA-PACIFIC` | Japan, Korea, Taiwan, Southeast Asia, the Philippines | 11.6 GB |
| `AS-RUSSIA-CENTRAL` | Siberia from the Urals to Lake Baikal | 4.8 GB |
| `AS-RUSSIA-EAST` | The Russian Far East | 6.4 GB |
| `OC-AUSTRALIA-NZ-PACIFIC` | Australia, New Zealand and the Pacific islands | 5.5 GB |

Sizes are download sizes. The whole world is about 161 GB. Antarctica is not available yet.

### 6. Run

```bash
xearthlayer run
```

## What we most want tested

### 1. The package manager

`xearthlayer packages` with no subcommand opens it. Local lists what is installed (an `↑` marks an available update), Library lists what you can install, and Progress shows each download and install as it happens.

**What to look for:** installing several regions at once, deleting one, refreshing with `r`, and quitting with `q` while jobs are running (it asks first, cancels cleanly, and a second `q` leaves at once). Anything that looks stuck, any row that never finishes, and any key that does not do what `?` says.

You can install new packages while `xearthlayer run` is active; they are used the next time `run` starts. Updating or deleting is refused while `run` is active, with a banner saying so. Before you try this, read the note on the log under How to report.

### 2. Faster installs that need less space

Downloads no longer wait for installs: the next package downloads while the previous one installs. Each package now extracts straight into place from its downloaded parts, so the temporary folder needs room for about the largest single download, not several times a package, and the install step itself is about twice as fast.

**What to look for:** how long a multi-region install takes, how much free space it needs, and what happens if you press Ctrl+C halfway (everything cancels, temporary files are removed, and the old version of a package being updated stays in place). If the temporary disk fills, a package shows "waiting for disk space" until room frees up.

### 3. macOS: signed builds and Homebrew

Gatekeeper should accept the binary as downloaded, from Safari, another browser or Homebrew, with no `xattr` step. Please report any security prompt word for word.

### 4. Carried over from alpha.1

Everything alpha.1 asked for still matters: no pauses or purple tiles at DSF boundary crossings (prefetch stands aside while X-Plane waits), night lighting over cities, the rebuilt scenery, and SimHeaven X-World Pro with `packages.xworld_pro` on.

### The dashboard

The Status pane leads its lines with emoji. If your terminal shows empty boxes instead, `xearthlayer config set tui.symbols plain` uses plain marks. The default, `auto`, tries to detect this for you.

## How to report

> **Copy the log first, before you run any other `xearthlayer` command.** In this build every command except `xearthlayer --version` empties the log when it starts, including `xearthlayer packages`, `xearthlayer config` and `xearthlayer diagnostics`. That includes opening the package manager while `xearthlayer run` is active, which empties the log of the flight in progress. It is tracked in [#320](https://github.com/samsoir/xearthlayer/issues/320).

The log is at `~/.local/state/xearthlayer/xearthlayer.log` on Linux and in `~/Library/Logs/XEarthLayer/` on macOS, unless you changed `logging.file`. Copy it somewhere safe, then run:

```bash
xearthlayer --version
xearthlayer diagnostics
```

The most useful report is your route, aircraft and flight time, the last few `Prefetch sample` lines from the copied log, and what looked wrong. For a package manager or install problem, say what you pressed and what the screen showed.

---

## Known issues, please don't report these

**Commands other than `run` empty the log.** See How to report above ([#320](https://github.com/samsoir/xearthlayer/issues/320)).

**`xearthlayer run` handles only Ctrl+C cleanly.** Closing its terminal or sending it SIGTERM does not unmount as cleanly yet ([#314](https://github.com/samsoir/xearthlayer/issues/314)).

**The package manager refreshes slowly with large packages installed.** After each install or delete it re-reads the installed list, which takes a while with a lot of scenery on disk. A spinner shows while it reads.

**FUSE read counts on the dashboard are low on macOS.** macOS serves repeat reads of a texture from its own cache, so XEarthLayer only sees the first one. Nothing else depends on that count.

**Antarctica is not in the library yet.**
